appraisal_events.evidence: "je suis trop bête… je paie avec mon argent le plaisir des autres"; "renonçons provisoirement aux gentillesses supplémentaires !"; and the narrator's analysis that "sa haine, tout comme son amour, ayant besoin de se manifester et d'agir il se plaisait à pousser de plus en plus loin ses imaginations mauvaises" so as to "avoir une occasion de la punir et d'assouvir sur elle sa rage grandissante"; he ends by wishing she might sprain her ankle or be driven off and kept "séquestrée".
appraisal_events.explanation: The narration lays bare Swann's mechanism — he feeds his own suspicions in order to earn the right to punish — and reduces the lover to a man rehearsing vengeful letters and grudging his money.

appraisal_events.evidence: Her letter asks him for the money to invite the Verdurins and their friends to Bayreuth: "De lui, elle ne disait pas un mot, il était sous-entendu que leur présence excluait la sienne." His prepared reply refuses, but "il sentait bien qu'avec l'argent qu'elle avait, ou qu'elle trouverait facilement, elle pourrait tout de même louer à Bayreuth".
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette asks Swann to fund a party from which he is silently excluded, and his one act of retaliation is immediately shown to be powerless to stop her going.

status_effects.explanation: He is shown petty and self-poisoning — calculating gifts, cultivating suspicions for the pleasure of punishing, wishing physical mishap on her.
The letter arrives exactly as he had imagined it, and his long-savoured refusal changes nothing: she will go without him and without his money.
He is placed outside the Bayreuth party he was asked to pay for — the letter does not mention him, and the guests' presence is understood to bar his own.
She sets the terms — asks for the money, omits him from the party, and can proceed without him whatever he answers — while he can only rage.

ambiguities: The passage closes by dissolving the hateful image and restoring "l'autre Odette", who prizes Swann's delicacy and trusts only him in grave matters; this softening qualifies but does not reverse a passage whose body is jealousy, calculation, and exclusion, so it is recorded here rather than as a countervailing event.
